decisions.reason: The source resolves the ESP32 header-pitch document mismatch and expands only the breakout Requirement's scope; it does not change GPIO assignments or their scope.
The source does not address I2C pull-ups, series resistors, cable length, bus speed, or applicability to the integrated board.
The header-pitch correction does not entail any change to the BOOT button, reset connection, capacitance, or their scope.
The source does not discuss panel inputs, their GPIO assignments, mounting, or integrated-board applicability.
The ESP32 breakout scope change does not alter the standalone USB supply, regulator capacity, power-source selection, or existing scope.
The source contains no decision about current-monitoring hardware, measured rails, measurement coverage, or the unresolved integrated-board monitor choice.
Although the source mentions the previous separate main board, local context shows that it refers specifically to the obsolete ESP32 header pitch in the PDF, not the mechanical-layout requirements.
The source does not change USB enumeration, programming behavior, interface choice, or the Requirement's scope.
Adding integrated-board scope to the ESP32 breakout does not cancel or modify the existing modular interboard connectors, pinouts, or topology.
The source does not address the panel power-button connector, PWRON wiring, control behavior, or integrated-board applicability.
The AXP2101 Requirement already has integrated-board scope, and the ESP32 header-pitch correction does not alter its battery, USB, or power-path state.
The source does not modify the separate sensor-board role, connector inventory, pinouts, or sensor-module interfaces.
